purpose: Date-scoped source review for the Bursa-Sakarya-Geyve-Lefke-Bilecik-İnegöl-Newşehir corridor. This artifact does not promote canonical political geometry.
principles: Political control is separate from settlement, military pressure, route use, and historical influence.
Later Ottoman administrative boundaries are not back-projected to 1326.
A source describing a conquest or route at an earlier date is evidence for historical change, not automatically a 1326 polygon boundary.
Where evidence is indirect or conflicting, keep the status unresolved rather than inventing geometry.

anchors.name: Bursa / Prusa
anchors.evidence: TDV states that Bursa surrendered to the Ottomans on 6 April 1326 after the long blockade; the castle and immediate strategic area received Turkish settlement while the Greek population was moved to lower parts of the city.

anchors.name: Nikaia / İznik
anchors.evidence: TDV dates the Ottoman capture to 2 March 1331 and describes the 1329 Pelekanon defeat as the event that determined the city's later fate.

anchors.name: Lefke / Osmaneli
anchors.evidence: TDV's Osman I account places Lefke among the Sakarya-valley fortifications captured during the early Ottoman expansion; the same account describes the 1304 campaign as closing routes to Nikaia.

anchors.name: Mekece
anchors.evidence: The Sakarya campaign evidence places Mekece among the positions taken by Osman during the 1304 campaign.

anchors.name: Geyve
anchors.evidence: TDV's Osman I account states that Geyve, Mekece, Absu and Lefke were taken in the 1304 Sakarya campaign; later source material continues to treat Geyve as a strategic passage.

anchors.name: Akhisar / Metabole area
anchors.evidence: TDV identifies Akhisar among the early Ottoman conquests and notes that Orhan used Akhisar as an operational center in 1305.

anchors.name: Bilecik / Belokome
anchors.evidence: TDV states that Bilecik was taken in 1299 and describes the town as a former Byzantine frontier center with a market serving both Greek and Turkmen populations.

anchors.name: İnegöl / Angelokomis
anchors.evidence: TDV's general Anatolia history lists İnegöl among the early Ottoman conquests. The Osman I account also places Angelokomis among settlements whose population fled during the early campaigns.

anchors.name: Harmankaya
anchors.politicalStatus1326: Ottoman-aligned frontier zone; exact jurisdiction unresolved
anchors.evidence: TDV identifies Köse Mihal as the Byzantine Harmankaya tekfur who became an Ottoman ally and Muslim around 1313 according to the Ottoman tradition. The exact territorial/legal status of Harmankaya on 7 April 1326 should not be inferred solely from this relationship.

anchors.name: Yenişehir / Melengeia
anchors.evidence: TDV's general Anatolia account says a Turkish town called Yenişehir was founded around 1301 after the early Ottoman conquests. TDV's Osman I account identifies Melengeia (Yenişehir) among areas depopulated during the 1304 campaign.

routeEvidence.note: TDV describes the early Ottoman migration and conflict geography around Söğüt, Domaniç and the İnegöl plain.

The 1304 campaign evidence identifies these positions as controlling the route system toward Nikaia. This should be represented as a network of route/control nodes rather than a modern-style straight border.
The historical conquest sequence establishes the chain of Ottoman-held centers, but a precise 1326 road geometry requires separate archaeological/topographic evidence.

negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.subject: Iznik approaches
negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.finding: The fact that Ottoman forces controlled surrounding positions before 1326 does not make Nikaia Ottoman. The city remained Byzantine until 1331.

negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.subject: Harmankaya
negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.finding: Köse Mihal's personal alignment should not be converted directly into a canonical province polygon.

negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.subject: Ancient roads
negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.finding: An ancient Roman route should not automatically be treated as an active 1326 road without medieval-use evidence.

negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.subject: Later Ottoman administration
negativeOrCautionaryEvidence.finding: Later Hüdavendigâr/Kocaeli administrative units are intentionally excluded from 1326 political geometry reconstruction.
